design_note: Looks-perfect match on faith, timelines, goals, and mutual attraction, but Person B’s stated growth orientation is subtly performative and contradicted by avoidance behaviors around conflict.

person_a.name: Tunde
person_a.summary: Senior product manager at a digital health startup in Seattle; calm, thoughtful, and playful with a steady, grounded presence.

values.faith: Christian (non-denominational); attends twice a month and sees faith as a practice of humility, service, and integrity; open to praying together but not dogmatic.
values.family: Close to siblings and cousins; Sunday FaceTimes are non-negotiable. Wants 2–3 kids and to split childcare equitably; values regular time with future in-laws.
values.career: Ambitious, but keeps boundaries (logs off by 6 most days). Career is a vehicle for impact, not identity; financially stable and tithes/volunteers.

attraction.stated_type: Warm, emotionally intelligent, community-oriented women who communicate directly and can laugh at themselves.
attraction.self_described_spark_with_b: We clicked right away—shared service mindset, similar church background, and easy banter. I felt seen by how curious and present she was.

emotional_profile.maturity: Names feelings in the moment and asks for clarity instead of assuming. In a prior 5-year relationship, co-created a budget and check-in ritual to handle friction; after a hard day he asks for a 20-minute decompression, then returns to connect. Friends call him the 'de-escalator.'
emotional_profile.attachment_style: Secure-leaning; reaches out when stressed rather than withdrawing. If a partner needs space, sets a specific check-in (e.g., tomorrow at 7) and follows through; comfortable with repair conversations and partner independence.
emotional_profile.growth_orientation: Two years with the same therapist focusing on family-of-origin patterns and conflict repair; can say 'I was wrong' without hedging. Took an NVC course and practices summarizing a partner's view before responding; keeps a monthly personal 'retro' where he writes what he learned and what he'll try differently.

person_a.life_stage: Homeowner in Seattle (Capitol Hill); hybrid work (3 days remote). Open to engagement in 12–18 months if aligned and kids in ~2–4 years. Flexible to shift neighborhoods if partner’s job requires.
dealbreakers: Dishonesty or cruelty in small moments (e.g., belittling waitstaff)
Substance misuse or routinely getting blackout drunk

person_b.name: Sofia
person_b.summary: Pediatric occupational therapist; upbeat, empathetic, and outdoorsy with a service-first mindset.

values.faith: Christian with Catholic roots; now at a progressive non-denominational church weekly and co-leads a small group. Sees faith as practiced compassion and community care.
values.family: Very close to her parents and younger brother; active aunt who wants 2 kids and values gentle parenting and Sunday family dinners.
values.career: Loves hands-on clinical work (plans 4 days/week long-term); protects evenings/weekends for relationships. Not chasing management unless it serves kids better.

attraction.stated_type: Emotionally available, steady men who lead with kindness and humor; admires nerdy doers who show up consistently.
attraction.self_described_spark_with_a: Talking to Tunde felt peaceful and light. We share service-oriented work and faith—could picture church then a farmer’s market. He listens without rushing to fix.

emotional_profile.maturity: Friends lean on me for calm perspective. In past relationships I initiated monthly 'state of us' check-ins; I jot notes before tough talks so I don’t react. When upset, I take a short walk and come back more centered.
emotional_profile.attachment_style: Earned-secure from earlier anxious patterns; I self-soothe and re-engage. With my ex, suggesting a shared calendar and routine check-ins reduced friction around plans.
emotional_profile.growth_orientation: I’m deeply committed to growth: I host a small book club on boundaries/NVC and I’ve been 'in therapy' for years. In the last 18 months I changed therapists four times because the fit wasn’t quite right—two felt too solution-focused, and one pushed me to sit with discomfort before I felt ready. After a conflict about finances with an ex, I suggested we pause the convo for the weekend to reflect, but we never found the right moment to circle back. When feedback gets heavy, I like to craft a thoughtful long note so I’m clear; sometimes that takes a couple of days, and by then the urgency has passed. I believe naming patterns heals them, and I’m working on not over-editing my feelings.

person_b.life_stage: Currently in Portland finishing a hospital contract; signed an offer at Seattle Children’s starting in 4 months and is apartment-hunting in Ballard. Open to engagement in 1–2 years and kids in ~2–4 years.
dealbreakers: Disrespect toward faith or community service
